name: Tobiano
summary: Tobiano: large white patches with sharp, fairly regular, often vertical edges that usually cross the topline, white on all four legs, a head that normally stays coloured, and often a tail of two colours. It is caused by a paracentric inversion on chromosome 3, between 42,737,476 and 79,471,993 on EquCab3.0: about 36.7 Mb (the often-quoted 43 Mb is an older, rounded estimate) that begins about 100 kb downstream of KIT, by the primary paper (Brooks et al. 2007; a 2024 review's word upstream is wrong), and probably disturbs how KIT is regulated; the KIT protein itself is unchanged. It is dominant: one copy is enough, and a horse with two copies is viable, passes it to every foal, and cannot be told from one with a single copy by its white: in about 760 photographed Paint Horses the median share of white was 36 per cent with two copies and 34 with one, ranging from 6 to 98 and from 4 to 79. Other white alleles add more: horses with one tobiano and one W20 copy had a median of 48 per cent. The inversion stops recombination across it, so KIT and MC1R (extension) are tightly linked in tobianos. Expression runs from the classic pattern through minimal tobiano to rare horses that look almost solid, so the pattern cannot always be told by eye. Small dark "ink spots" inside the white are associated with tobiano but are not explained by the genotype alone. The KIT boosters W20, W32, W34 and W35 can add white to it. It lies over any base colour and is not linked to lethal white, which belongs to frame overo. Common in Paints, Pintos, Shetlands, Miniatures, Warmbloods, Gypsy horses, Icelandic Horses and Paso Finos; uncommon in Quarter Horses, Thoroughbreds, Standardbreds and Arabians. UC Davis writes the genotypes N/N, N/TO and TO/TO. No effect on build, performance or health is established.

phenotypes.name: Tobiano
phenotypes.description: White patches with sharp, fairly regular, often vertical edges that usually cross the topline between the ears and the tail; white on all four legs, usually below the knees and hocks; a head that normally stays coloured; and often a tail of two colours. The white is white hair over pink skin. Eyes are usually brown, though one or both may be blue or partly blue. The amount of white varies from extensive to minimal, and rare horses look almost solid. One copy and two copies give the same pattern; two copies average very slightly more white, but the ranges overlap almost entirely.
